article.story: Virginia (4-4) at No. 14 Wake Forest (6-1), Oct. 31 at 3:45 p.m. EDT. Opening Line: Wake Forest by 14. Against the spread: Wake Forest 5-2, Virginia 3-5. How to watch: ESPN2 Key stats Wake Forest Offense Overall: 445.9 yards per game (25th in FBS) Passing: 290.3 yards per game (13th) Rushing: 155.6 yards per game (69th) Scoring: 37.4 points per game (14th) Wake Forest Defense Overall: 322.6 yards per game (35th in FBS) Passing: 230.1 yards per game (100th) Rushing: 92.4 yards per game (11th) Scoring: 19.4 points per game (30th) Virginia Offense Overall: 361.6 yards per game (94th in FBS) Passing: 200.0 yards per game (98th) Rushing: 161.6 yards per game (62nd) Scoring: 28.3 points per game (71st) Virginia Defense Overall: 326.6 yards per game (42nd in FBS) Passing: 184.1 yards per game (32nd) Rushing: 142.5 yards per game (71st) Scoring: 19.6 points per game (31st) Wake Forest ranks 18th in FBS in third down percentage, converting 48.9% of the time. Wake Forest ranks 134th in the FBS averaging 84.1 penalty yards per game, compared to Virginia's 32nd-ranked 46.9 per-game average. Virginia is 112th in FBS in red zone defense, allowing opponents to score on 89.5% of trips. Wake Forest's red zone offense ranks 13th, scoring on 93.9% of red zone opportunities. Wake Forest ranks 107th in the FBS with an average time of possession of 28:38, compared to Virginia's 30th-ranked average of 32:03. Team leaders Wake Forest Passing: Gio Lopez, 1,947 yards, 17 TDs, 1 INT, 67.6 completion percentage Rushing: Ty Clark, 328 yards on 70 carries, 4 TDs Receiving: Carlos Hernandez, 720 yards on 49 catches, 4 TDs Virginia Passing: Beau Pribula, 1,375 yards, 13 TDs, 2 INTs, 65.0 completion percentage Rushing: Jekail Middlebrook, 513 yards on 105 carries, 4 TDs Receiving: Dashawn Martin, 253 yards on 17 catches, 5 TDs Last game Wake Forest defeated Cal 41-7 on Oct. 17. Lopez threw for 267 yards on 16-of-23 attempts (69.6%) with four touchdowns and no interceptions. He also carried the ball eight times for 51 yards. Jamar Searcy carried the ball five times for 61 yards and scored one touchdown. Dominick Barry had four receptions for 102 yards and three touchdowns. Virginia lost 19-16 to Duke on Oct. 23. Pribula led Virginia with 158 yards on 15-of-24 passing (62.5%) for no touchdowns and one interception. He also carried the ball 21 times for 66 yards. Middlebrook carried the ball 24 times for 117 yards and scored one touchdown, adding two receptions for eight yards. John Rogers put up 65 yards on five catches. Next game Wake Forest hosts Merrimack on Nov. 7. Virginia hosts Cal on Nov. 14.
